claim: Starting from a smooth bell (Gaussian or cosine bump) instead of the constant and then hill-climbing on the heights raises R from the constant's 2/3 to about 0.79-0.80; the best single run reached 0.7952 with a Gaussian seed (s in 15-30) plus multiplicative hill-climbing on N=200, and a cosine-bump multi-stage search reached 0.8328.

A cosine-bump start with coordinate ascent and perturbed restarts (N=50) gave the generation's best score, 0.8328 (+0.1662 over the constant), with 24% of heights zero and a fatter f*f top (16.8% of knots within 0.1% of the max vs 2.7% for the Gaussian-seeded run).

Generalized Gaussian exp(-|x|^p) scanned over p=1.0-3.0 with scale variants and hill-climbing only reached 0.7933, below the plain Gaussian-seeded run's 0.7952; no p away from 2 gave a clear gain, so the p-family did not beat the Gaussian.

Smoothed-box seeds (erf-based, a in 0-2.0, w in 0.15-1.2) plus hill-climbing reached only 0.7875, the weakest of the three deep runs; the flat-topped family did not push f*f closer to a plateau than the Gaussian.

Does the win come from the seed shape or from the search? The cosine-bump run (p0004) beat the Gaussian-seeded run (p0005) at much coarser N (50 vs 200) with 24% zeros, suggesting a compact, partly-zero support may help; worth testing cosine-bump seeds at several N with the same hill-climber to separate seed from search.

Very fine grids did not help: N=3200 with progressive upsampling scored 0.7449 and N=800 with block hill-climbing scored 0.7863, both below the N=50 cosine-bump run's 0.8328; whether coarse N (50-200) is genuinely better than fine N under a fixed budget is worth a controlled test.

Upsampling p0004's N=50 asymmetric heights to N=100 via linear interpolation and re-polishing (coordinate ascent + perturbed restarts) raised R from 0.832821 to 0.833771 (+0.00095), the best score so far; the f*f peak moved from 0.390 to 0.545 of the support and ||f*f||_inf dropped from 1.1475 to 1.1436 while ||f*f||_2^2 stayed ~0.9535, so finer structure does help slightly at N=100.

Replacing p0004's single-index perturbation stage with full coordinate ascent (halving step) plus block/ramp perturbations at the same N=50 gave +0.000001 (0.832821 -> 0.832822): the N=50 optimum was already locally saturated, so block/segment moves found nothing new at that resolution.

Resampling the Gaussian-seeded N=200 solution to N=800 before multiplicative single-coordinate hill-climbing gave exactly 0.795235 (no change) and the output stayed at N=200 with 0% zeros and a symmetric f*f peak at 0.487; finer grid alone does not move the Gaussian line, consistent with F6 that fine grids don't help.

Cyclic coordinate ascent with multiplicative+additive moves, progressive upsampling and block-noise restarts on the N=3200 line raised R from 0.744910 to 0.759601 (+0.01469) but still stayed well below the coarse-N asymmetric runs (0.83); the f*f top remained sharp (2.09% of knots within 0.1% of max) and 0% zeros, so fine-grid search improves its own baseline without reaching the coarse-N regime.

Two gen-2 programs crashed before producing a score: p0009 (block-averaging p0005 to N=50 then running p0004's search) died with 'ValueError: The weights and list don't have the same length' in np.bincount, and p0011 (analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B ascent) died with "NameError: name 'n' is not defined" in the correlation slicing; neither the search-vs-seed test (F5) nor the gradient-based ascent was a

The best solutions are asymmetric with the f*f peak off-centre (0.390 at N=50, 0.545 at N=100) and ~23-24% zero heights, while every symmetric seed (Gaussian, cosine, smoothed box) stalls at 0.79-0.80 with a centred peak; whether asymmetry is the causal ingredient (vs. a byproduct of the coarse-N search) is still untested, since the direct search-vs-seed test p0009 crashed.

An exact analytic gradient of R (with finite-difference check) plus projected-gradient ascent, then structured large perturbations with a gradient inner loop, escaped p0012's N=100 basin and raised R from 0.833771 to 0.847584 (+0.0138) at N=200; the f*f peak moved off-centre to 0.575 and the 1%-of-max knot share rose to 26.4%. This is the largest single gain of the generation and shows the bottlen

A sparse sum-of-K-boxes construction (3K parameters, K=3-6, random search then Powell refine at N=100, then coordinate ascent at N=200) reached 0.848602 from scratch, the best score of the generation and above the gradient-perturbation run p0017 (0.847584). The box family produces a flatter f*f top (32.7% of knots within 1% of max vs 26.4% for p0017) and only 10% zero heights, so a structured few-

Gradient ascent alone, without large structured perturbations, barely moved the score: p0018 added the exact gradient and projected-gradient ascent at N=100 then N=200 but gained only +0.000047 (0.833771 -> 0.833818). The local basin is already sharp; the gain in p0017 came from the perturbation/restart loop, not from the gradient itself.

Resampling to finer N and re-running coordinate/block search on the coarse-N optimum gave no real gain: p0015 (resample p0010 up to 8x N, randomized coordinate order, block perturbations) scored 0.832823 (+0.000001) and p0014 (exact multi-step coordinate descent plus block/bump restarts at N=50) scored 0.832821 (+0.000000). The N=50 basin is exhausted regardless of search schedule.

Fine grids with smooth seeds still stall near 0.79: p0016 resampled p0002 to N=1200 and ran multi-scale block-multiplicative hill climbing with restarts, reaching only 0.788222 (+0.0019) with 0% zeros and a centred-ish peak at 0.386. Fine-N smooth-seeded search remains far below the coarse-N asymmetric/box line (0.848).

Two distinct high-scoring families now exist: the gradient-perturbation line from p0012 (p0017, 0.8476, 22.5% zeros, peak at 0.575) and the box-sum line (p0019, 0.8486, 10% zeros, peak at 0.615). Both are asymmetric with off-centre f*f peaks. Worth testing whether seeding the box-sum solution into the gradient-perturbation loop (or vice versa) combines their gains, and whether the box family at hi

Giving the box-sum line (p0019, 0.8486) the exact-gradient PGD + structured-perturbation loop (segment scale, Gaussian bump, zeroing, reversal) plus an N=400 upsampling stage raised R from 0.848602 to 0.868524 (+0.0199), the best score of the generation; the f*f 1%-of-max knot share rose to 34.3% and the peak sits at 0.757 of the support. The cheap local search, not the box parametrization, was th

Compressing p0017's N=200 free-form heights into K=8 boxes, Powell-fitting the box parameters, then expanding back to N=200 and running PGD polish with perturbations raised R from 0.847584 to 0.865848 (+0.0183). The box fit alone did not lose ground, so the box structure is a representable route into p0017's basin rather than a separate family; the result keeps 24.5% zeros and an off-centre peak a

Widening the box family to K up to 12 with independent left/right erf ramp widths (5K params), seeded from p0019's layout and refined by Powell at N=100 then N=200 plus coordinate ascent, raised R from 0.848602 to 0.851064 (+0.0025). The gain is real but small and the shape changed character (zeros 8%->12%, peak pushed to 0.810, max/mean height 2.73), so extra box degrees of freedom help modestly

Adding the exact-gradient PGD to p0019's box construction without the deep perturbation/upsampling schedule (wide-loop p0025) gained only +0.000807 (0.848602 -> 0.849410), versus +0.0199 for the deep version p0024. Gradient ascent alone on the box basin is nearly saturated; the large structured perturbations and N=400 stage carry most of p0024's gain.

Gradient PGD plus multi-resolution coordinate polishing on the p0012 line (wide-loop p0020) gained only +0.000178 (0.833771 -> 0.833949) even at N=300, confirming that the N=100 gradient-perturbation basin is locally saturated and needs the large structured perturbations of p0017/p0024 to move, not more polishing.

Multi-scale coordinate ascent with an N-growth schedule (200->3200) and perturbed restarts on the smooth Gaussian-seeded line (wide-loop p0021) reached only 0.796669 (+0.0014 over 0.795235) with 0% zeros and a near-centred peak at 0.461. Fine grids and smooth seeds remain stuck near 0.79-0.80 regardless of search strength, so the gap to 0.86+ is structural (asymmetry plus zeros), not a search-effo

Giving the PGD+structured-perturbation loop a full budget at N=400 (skipping the N=200 stages that ate 21 of p0024's 28 s) and widening the move set from 4 to 7 types (adding flatten and sub-block shift, plus annealing acceptance and periodic N=800 PGD probes) raised R from 0.868524 to 0.872542 (+0.0040), the best score so far; the result ended at N=800 with 10.9% zeros, peak at 0.680, and 15.8% o

Replacing the exact max in the gradient by an annealed log-sum-exp softmax (spreading correction over near-max knots instead of only the argmax) plus the exact PGD and perturbation loop raised R from 0.868524 to 0.870986 (+0.0025); the f*f top got markedly flatter (0.1%-of-max knot share 15.8% -> 33.8%), confirming the myopic-max diagnosis.

Building a flat f*f directly from a sparse spike train (K=30 annealed spike centers chosen to flatten the pairwise-sum histogram, then PGD polish) scored only 0.657833, below the constant's 0.666667: 96.5% zeros, max/mean 36.2, and only 2.5% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max. The flat-histogram construction did not survive the polish and is not a viable route at this budget.

Replacing p0019's Powell/coordinate box search with exact-gradient ascent plus coordinate ascent and perturb-restart lost ground: R fell from 0.848602 to 0.847022 (-0.0016) at N=200 with only 2.0% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max. Gradient ascent alone is a weaker local search than Powell on the box-parameter family.

Pushing the PGD line to higher resolution (stages up to N=2000 with PGD, coordinate polish, small-noise perturbations) gained only +0.000369 (0.868524 -> 0.868893) and the peak drifted to 0.449 with 10.0% of f*f knots within 0.1% of max; fine grids still do not beat the coarse-N asymmetric basin.

An upsampling-to-N=400 PGD program with sinusoidal perturbations and an N=1200 final refinement crashed with 'ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (200,) (400,)': the sinusoidal perturbation was added to a length-200 array using a length-400 index. Mixing arrays of different N in the perturbation stage is a recurring crash mode.
